cases.case_summary: An 8-year-old girl presented to the pediatric emergency department with 5 days of intermittent fever, followed by abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
cases.full_text:
An 8-year-old girl presented to the pediatric emergency department with 5 days of intermittent fever, followed by abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
Respiratory symptoms: No cough, congestion, or rhinorrhea
Temperature: 38.6 °C
Eye, oral, and skin examination: Bilateral nonpurulent conjunctivitis, erythematous throat, palmar erythema, strawberry tongue, and erythema multiform rash, without hypotension
Lymph node, lung, and cardiac examination: No lymphadenopathy or retraction breathing, normal respiratory sounds, no focal signs of infection, and an II/VI murmur on the left sternal border
Laboratory studies: Urinalysis and urine culture negative; ESR 67 mm/h; CRP 166 mg/L; platelets 192 × 10^9/L; hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL; WBC 10.3 × 10^9/L (PMN 82%); routine biochemistry and liver function tests normal
Echocardiography: No pathology related to the coronary arteries
COVID-19 RT-PCR and blood culture: COVID-19 RT-PCR and blood culture negative
COVID-19 serology: Positive, with serum COVID-19 IgM of 2.1

cases.case_summary: A 62-year-old man presented to ENT with more frequent ear infections and cerumen impaction.
cases.full_text:
A 62-year-old man presented to ENT with more frequent ear infections and cerumen impaction.
Otoscopy: Significant bilateral external auditory canal narrowing, greater on the right, preventing visualisation of the tympanic membrane.
History of cerumen removal: Removal of impacted cerumen had often been difficult enough to require anaesthesia because of discomfort.
History of ear canal bony outgrowths: He had known of bony outgrowths for 30 years and had previously declined offered surgery.
Diving history: Daily free diving during the summer months from early teens into late adulthood, with less participation over the past 15 years.
Ear protection while diving: No swimming cap or ear plugs were used while diving.
High-resolution CT of the temporal bones: Bilateral dense sessile outgrowths arising from the osseous external auditory canal and occluding the canal on axial and coronal images.
High-resolution CT canal lumen: Bilateral broad-based focal circumferential bony overgrowths of the osseous external auditory canals, with residual luminal diameter 1–2 mm.
High-resolution CT soft tissue and bone: No soft tissue density in either canal and no bony erosion.

cases.case_summary: A 9-year-old girl presented to the emergency room with chest pain and dyspnea.
cases.full_text:
A 9-year-old girl presented to the emergency room with chest pain and dyspnea.
Recent illness and chest trauma: She had recovered from a recent upper respiratory infection and had minor trauma to the anterior chest wall from a fall a week prior.
Leukocyte and absolute eosinophil count: Leukocyte count 12,000 cells/µL, with absolute eosinophil count 1,570 cells/µL (normal 40–190 cells/µL).
Cardiac troponin T: 0.25 ng/mL (normal <0.1 ng/mL).
Echocardiography: Moderate-sized circumferential pericardial effusion, right atrial collapse, normal inflow and outflow variability across valves, normal biventricular systolic function, and no ventricular septal defect.
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: Myocardial global T2 70 ms, native myocardial global T1 1150 ms, increased left ventricular wall thickness, moderate-sized pericardial effusion, and no myocardial late gadolinium enhancement.
Exposure history: Pica and exposure to two dogs and a cat in the home.
Chest computed tomography: Multiple pulmonary nodules with adjacent ground glass opacities.
Toxocara serology: Toxocara antibody positive twelve days into the illness.

cases.case_summary: A 60-year-old man presented with a 4-hour history of acute right lower abdominal pain.
cases.full_text:
A 60-year-old man presented with a 4-hour history of acute right lower abdominal pain.
Past history: Emphysema, hypertension, heavy cigarette smoking, and prostate cancer in remission.
Abdominal examination: Peritonism in the right lower quadrant.
Abdominal CT: Perforated appendix with a 51 × 31 × 26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding, innumerable hepatic nodules, mural thickening of the caecum and sigmoid colon, marked mesenteric, para-aortic and portocaval lymphadenopathy, and pulmonary consolidation/collapse in the right lower lobe.
Chest CT: On day two after laparotomy, bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy contiguous with soft tissue thickening enveloping the right lower lobe and middle lobe bronchi.
Appendix histology: Lesional cells with small cell morphology: round to oval, scant cytoplasm, poorly defined cell borders, hyperchromatic nuclei, occasional inconspicuous nucleoli, nuclear moulding, and frequent mitotic figures.
Immunohistochemistry: TTF1 positive, p53 over expression, loss of RB1, CD56 positive, and negative for CXD2.
Neuroendocrine marker immunohistochemistry: Positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin A and CD56.
Bronchoalveolar lavage cytology: The same cells were demonstrated in bronchoalveolar lavage cytology.

cases.case_summary: A 24-year-old woman presented with a labial mass that had emerged 12 years earlier and grown gradually, without pain or discomfort until recently.
cases.full_text:
A 24-year-old woman presented with a labial mass that had emerged 12 years earlier and grown gradually, without pain or discomfort until recently.
Menstrual history: Menarche at age 11 years, with a regular menstrual cycle.
History of the labial mass: A labial mass had emerged 12 years earlier, grown gradually, and caused no pain or discomfort until recently.
Examination of the labial mass: Pedunculated mass in the upper left labium measuring 75 × 44 mm, resembling a penis, with relatively soft texture, normal skin temperature, clear boundaries, and no ulceration.
Association of the lesion with menstruation: Progressive growth was not connected with the menstrual cycle, and the lesion was asymptomatic during menstruation.
Breast, abdominal, and lymph node examination: Breast and abdominal examinations were normal. Axillary and supraclavicular lymph nodes could not be palpated. There was no pain on palpation and no enlarged groin lymph nodes.
Ultrasonography of the lesion: Hyperechoic mass with clearly defined margins, internal echoes, and fibroglandular tissue, measuring 70 × 40 mm.
Pelvic ultrasound: No abnormality in the uterus or ovaries.
Histopathology of the resected mass: Breast acini and ducts lined with epithelial and myoepithelial cells.

cases.case_summary: A 34-year-old woman presented with pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar.
cases.full_text:
A 34-year-old woman presented with pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar.
Prior treatment of the mandibular right first molar: Endodontically treated almost 5 years before presentation.
Percussion of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar: Pain on percussion of both teeth.
Inspection of overlying skin and mucosa: Skin and mucosa normal, without ulceration, erythema, suppuration, or increased temperature.
Palpation of the lingual and buccal cortices: Bony hard consistency on both lingual and buccal cortices.
Orthopantomography: Uniloculated radiolucent lesion engulfing the apices of the mandibular right second premolar and an endodontically treated first molar, extending to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal, with an irregular shape.
Cone beam computed tomography: Buccolingual extension almost completely obliterating the lingual cortex; the lesion measured 23.4 × 14.2 × 6.6 mm at its peaks.
Microscopy of the incisional biopsy: Fibroconnective tissue with a few crushed bone particles, severe infiltration by acute inflammatory cells, and some foamy macrophages.
Microscopy of the suppurative exudate: Colonies of filamentous bacteria as round basophilic masses with a radial configuration resembling sulfur granules.

cases.case_summary: A man presents with a tender, ulcerated plaque on the right medial knee and thigh.
cases.full_text:
A man presents with a tender, ulcerated plaque on the right medial knee and thigh.
Prior knee injury: The plaque arose at a healed abrasion from 2 decades earlier, when he entered the Chesapeake Bay and scraped his knee on a rock.
Longstanding plaque: The plaque remained about 4 cm for decades until new tenderness led him to seek dermatologic care.
Course before referral: The plaque worsened over the next 3 years, and he was referred for care.
Vital signs: Vital signs were normal.
Skin examination: The right medial knee and thigh had a tender, indurated, violaceous, ulcerated plaque with irregular borders, approximately 10 cm in diameter.
Skin biopsy microbial PCR and culture: PCR and culture demonstrated Mycobacterium marinum and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Acid-fast bacilli stain: Acid-fast bacilli staining of the skin biopsy was positive.
Skin biopsy histopathology: Necrotizing vasculitis of dermal blood vessels with vascular and extravascular granulomas.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sudden increase in dyspnea after one month of exertional dyspnea, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent fever, and develops acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest with pulseless electrical activity.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sudden increase in dyspnea after one month of exertional dyspnea, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent fever, and develops acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest with pulseless electrical activity.
Recent symptom history: One-month history of dyspnea on exertion, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent unquantified fever.
Emergency department course: Acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest with pulseless electrical activity; difficult to ventilate despite orotracheal intubation.
Vital signs on arrival: Blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36 °C, and oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support.
Physical examination: Anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm), thick neck with jugular engorgement and no masses, no skin lesions, sinus tachycardia, bilateral thick rales, and no abdominal collateral circulation, ascites, masses, or extremity edema.
Chest radiography: Homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the airway to the left.
Fiberoptic bronchoscopy: Extrinsic compression at the distal end of the orotracheal tube, with no endotracheal or endobronchial lesions.
Chest and neck CT: Lobulated solid mass in the right thoracic operculum, 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm, described as seeming to originate in the pleura, with a 27 × 28 mm nodular component on the mediastinal pleura; mass effect on the right pulmonary hilum, right supra-aortic trunks, and superior vena cava; pneumomediastinum and left pneumothorax; lytic involvement of the T1 and T2 vertebral bodies, pedicles, and transverse processes with anterior cortical fracture.
Biopsy histopathology: Mesenchymal lesion with abundant randomly arranged osteoclast-type giant cells with round nuclei and mild pleomorphism; spindle cells with cytological atypia, an increased nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, and abundant mitoses; isolated osteoid; tumor and ischemic necrosis; no normal bone; Ki-67 index 18%; phosphorylated histone H3 with three mitoses per high-power field.

cases.case_summary: A 41-year-old man, previously well, presented with a 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough, along with worsening chronic lower back pain and a painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux.
cases.full_text:
A 41-year-old man, previously well, presented with a 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough, along with worsening chronic lower back pain and a painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux.
Prior symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for back pain, and antibacterial cream for the toe ulcer
Physical examination: Normotensive, apyretic, and cachectic, with no peripheral lymphadenopathy or oedema
Urine protein-creatinine ratio: 0.242 g/mmol creatinine
Urine dipstick and microscopy: 3+ leucocytes and 3+ red blood cells; granular casts; no bacterial culture growth
Serum immunoglobulin A: 6.2 g/L (normal range 0.7–4 g/L)
Autoimmune and infection serology: Anti-DNase B 259 IU/ml (normal range less than 200 IU/ml); antinuclear antibodies, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies negative; HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and syphilis negative
Kidney biopsy light microscopy: 59 glomeruli, 4 globally sclerosed, 3 segmentally sclerosed, and 1 cellular crescent; diffuse mesangial hypercellularity without endocapillary hypercellularity; no double contours or spikes; Congo red stain with no amyloid
Kidney biopsy immunohistochemistry: Diffuse strong mesangial IgA (3+) with lesser paramesangial staining; IgM and C3 weak (1+); IgG and C1q negative

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old man presented in late January with painful tingling in his toes and purple-black discoloration of the toes of both feet, beginning 3 weeks earlier.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old man presented in late January with painful tingling in his toes and purple-black discoloration of the toes of both feet, beginning 3 weeks earlier.
Toe symptoms: Painful tingling in the toes beginning 3 weeks earlier, followed by purple/black discoloration of the toes of both feet.
Activity before symptom onset: A skiing trip approximately one week before the symptoms started.
Other symptoms and past history: Some fatigue, with no other symptoms and no other past medical history.
Examination of the toes: Flat purple/red lesions on the plantar aspects of the first through third toes, bilaterally.
Effect of warming: The lesions improved but did not completely disappear with warming.
Laboratory studies: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 5; ANA, rheumatoid factor, antiphospholipid antibodies, and cryoglobulins negative.
Echocardiogram and abdominal ultrasound: No source of embolism.
Punch biopsy of a toe lesion: Superficial and deep perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates with focal dermal hemorrhage and mild dermal edema; no vasculitis.

cases.case_summary: A 30-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of worsening crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea.
cases.full_text:
A 30-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of worsening crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea.
Home medication: Progesterone-only contraceptive for the past 2 months and no other medication
Abdominal examination: Normal bowel sounds and diffuse tenderness to palpation, without guarding or rigidity
Blood tests: Normal complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and coagulation panel; C-reactive protein 4.8
Stool studies: Negative cultures and negative Clostridioides difficile toxins
Fecal calprotectin: 2006 mcg/g (reference range 10–50 mcg/g)
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis: Mild colonic wall thickening and adjacent inflammatory changes involving the mid and descending colon, without perforation or abscess
Colonoscopy: Segmental erythema and ulceration involving the descending and sigmoid colon; ascending colon, transverse colon, and rectum normal-appearing
Colonic biopsy histopathology: Subepithelial edema and hemorrhage, with no granulomas or dysplasia

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old Hispanic man presented with prostatism that had progressed over 3 months.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old Hispanic man presented with prostatism that had progressed over 3 months.
Presenting symptoms: Prostatism progressing over 3 months
Digital rectal examination: Enlarged gland with a soft nodule in the left lobe
Prostate-specific antigen: 3.4 ng/mL, within normal limits
Gross examination of the prostatectomy specimen: 4.5 × 4 × 2 cm, 27 g, multinodular and elastic, with a well-defined blackish area 1.4 cm in diameter in the left lobe
Histologic examination: Dusty and granular melanin pigment within stromal myofibroblasts on hematoxylin and eosin stain
Masson-Fontana stain: Positive; highlights pigmented stromal cells and confirms melanin
Iron stain: Negative in the pigmented stromal cells
S-100 immunohistochemistry: Pigmented stromal cells immunopositive for S100 protein

cases.case_summary: A 45-year-old Caucasian man presented with a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump for three weeks and low-grade fever (37.5°C to 38°C) over the past week.
cases.full_text:
A 45-year-old Caucasian man presented with a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump for three weeks and low-grade fever (37.5°C to 38°C) over the past week.
Left axillary lump: Tender, slow-growing left axillary lump for three weeks
Fever: Low-grade fever of 37.5°C to 38°C for the last week
Physical examination: Tender, non-mobile 3×4 cm left axillary lymphadenopathy; examination otherwise unremarkable
Family history: No family history of lymphoproliferative or autoimmune disease
Laboratory studies: Normal and/or negative, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, coagulation tests, blood glucose, creatinine, uric acid, sodium, potassium, lipids, liver parameters, cytokeratin, lactate dehydrogenase, ferritin, serum C3 and C4, antinuclear antibody, rheumatoid factor, C-reactive protein, thyroid-stimulating hormone, urine tests, and serology for herpes simplex virus 1 and 2, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C virus, toxoplasma, human herpes virus 8, parvovirus B19, human immunodeficiency virus 1, and human T-lymphotropic virus type 1
Thoracoabdominal computed tomography: Normal except for the axillary lymphadenopathy
Lymph node biopsy: Coagulative necrosis and frequent karyorrhexis with a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
Mycobacterial investigation: Negative

cases.case_summary: A 36-year-old man presents to the hospital after an episode of presyncope. He felt dizzy in the bathroom, lay down, and the dizziness subsided after 15 minutes.
cases.full_text:
A 36-year-old man presents to the hospital after an episode of presyncope. He felt dizzy in the bathroom, lay down, and the dizziness subsided after 15 minutes.
Recent symptoms: No previous similar episodes, seizure-like activity, postictal state, or incontinence. He denied weight loss, night sweats, and high-grade fever, and reported one episode of chills a few hours before presentation.
Physical examination: Mild tachycardia, a soft grade II/VI systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border, and splinter hemorrhages in the nail beds. The rest of the examination, including the neurologic examination, was normal.
Transthoracic echocardiography: Mitral valve vegetation measuring 0.8 cm × 0.6 cm.
Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis: Multiple lytic bone lesions, splenic and renal infarcts, evidence of malignant ascites, and omental caking.
Omental fine-needle aspiration: Adenocarcinoma.
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsy: Gastric ulcer at the greater curvature in the gastric body; biopsies showed undifferentiated gastric adenocarcinoma.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging: Acute right middle cerebral artery stroke.
Blood cultures: Serial blood cultures remained negative after 17 days of incubation.

cases.case_summary: A 40-year-old woman is admitted to the emergency room with abdominal pain and vomiting, and she has passed no gas or stool for two days.
cases.full_text:
A 40-year-old woman is admitted to the emergency room with abdominal pain and vomiting, and she has passed no gas or stool for two days.
Prior abdominal operation: Hysterectomy through a Pfannenstiel incision four years earlier
Abdominal symptoms since that operation: Occasional abdominal pain since the operation
Temperature and vital signs: No fever; vital signs stable
Abdominal palpation: An 8 cm mass palpated in the epigastric region
Blood analyses: Leukocytosis; the other blood analyses were normal
Plain abdominal radiography: Air-fluid levels in a few intestinal loops and multiple opaque substances accumulated as a strip in the midline
Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography: A mass among small-bowel loops measuring 107 × 60 mm at the L2–4 level, closely related to the anterior abdominal wall, with linear metallic hypodense artefacts in its right half and peripheral contrast enhancement
Opened operative specimen: A laparotomy pad with radiopaque markers inside the capsule

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old perimenopausal woman presents with worsening abdominal distention, abdominal tenderness, and constipation for over 3 weeks.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old perimenopausal woman presents with worsening abdominal distention, abdominal tenderness, and constipation for over 3 weeks.
Past medical and surgical history: Hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, and cesarean section with bilateral tubal ligation; no smoking history; family history noncontributory.
Abdominal examination: Vital signs within normal limits; abdomen distended and diffusely tender.
Pelvic examination: A 30 cm adnexal mass; the uterus was small and difficult to palpate because of the mass.
Transvaginal and transabdominal ultrasound with color Doppler: Large pelvic mass, described as likely arising from the left ovary and extending to the first intercostal space; multiloculated complex mass with multiple thick septations measuring 24 × 18 cm; moderate pelvic free fluid; anteverted uterus of normal appearance with a thin endometrial lining; right ovary 3.9 × 3.3 × 3.5 cm with a 3 cm simple cyst.
Computed tomography: A 28.3 × 24.4 × 16.3 cm predominantly cystic mass extending from the pelvis to the upper abdomen, with superior displacement of the bowel.
CA125: Value of 95, reported as significantly elevated.
Intraoperative findings: Uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries were normal. A 26–28 cm multiloculated peritoneal cyst arose from the left cornual region of the uterine fundus on a wide pedicle, with significant adhesions to the ureters, omentum, and pelvic sidewall. Three liters of cystic fluid were evacuated.
Cyst fluid cytology: Reactive benign mesothelial cells.

cases.case_summary: A 54-year-old woman was brought by her family to the neurosurgical emergency department with rapid, progressive mental confusion that had begun about two months earlier, with significant worsening over the last two weeks, leaving her completely dependent for basic daily activities such as bathing and eating.
cases.full_text:
A 54-year-old woman was brought by her family to the neurosurgical emergency department with rapid, progressive mental confusion that had begun about two months earlier, with significant worsening over the last two weeks, leaving her completely dependent for basic daily activities such as bathing and eating.
Past medical history: Controlled arterial hypertension; no other significant condition reported.
General and neurological examination: Normotensive but in poor general condition; able only to obey simple orders; restricted to bed, with gait not evaluated because of general weakness; seemed to have no motor deficits; no cranial nerve alterations and no meningeal signs. A complete examination was limited by her general condition. Karnofsky performance score 50.
Brain MRI: Two left occipital lesions surrounded by edema.
Preoperative complete blood count, chest radiography, and electrocardiogram: No abnormalities.
Histopathology of the resected lesion: Multiple fungi in the deeper part of the lesion and multiple inflammatory cells on hematoxylin-eosin staining.
HIV and hepatitis tests: No HIV or hepatitis; both tests were performed twice.
Chest and abdominal CT: Normal.
Cerebrospinal fluid examination: Large numbers of Cryptococcus neoformans and increased protein.

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old wheelchair-bound man presented with severe back pain and an inability to walk for the past two weeks.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old wheelchair-bound man presented with severe back pain and an inability to walk for the past two weeks.
Recent back pain and trauma history: No history of significant trauma; minor back pain began after pulling a rug one month earlier.
Back and leg symptom course: Pain that was initially mild gradually became severely disabling, with progressive weakness and diffuse paresthesia in both legs.
Standing, lower-limb strength, and sphincter function: He could hardly stand. Big-toe extensors were weak bilaterally (severe on the left, moderate on the right), and ankle dorsiflexors were moderately weak on both sides. Sphincter function was intact. Ankle plantar flexors and quadriceps had normal power.
Laboratory testing: C-reactive protein was raised and was reported as the only significant laboratory finding.
Lumbosacral radiographs: Compression fracture of L2 and burst fracture of L5 with canal compromise and an intravertebral vacuum cleft at L5.
Lumbar MRI: At L5, axial images showed a linear area of decreased signal intensity within an area of increased signal intensity.
Paraspinal soft tissue and whole-body bone scan: No paravertebral soft-tissue mass or abscess. Bone scan uptake was increased only in the two affected vertebral areas.
Vertebral bone microscopy: Trabecular bone fragments with bony sequestrum, new bone formation, and necrosis.

cases.case_summary: A 32-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks and 3 days of gestation presented acutely with left lower abdominal pain and vomiting.
cases.full_text:
A 32-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks and 3 days of gestation presented acutely with left lower abdominal pain and vomiting.
Pelvic ultrasound: Left ovarian cyst measured 70 × 55 × 60 mm, with internal echoes and an avascular solid component, at 32 weeks.
Abdominal examination: Observations were stable and she appeared clinically well. There was slight tenderness on the left side of the abdomen without guarding, and the uterus was soft and relaxed.
Admission blood tests: Haemoglobin 121 g/L, white cell count 10.0 × 10^9/L, platelets 270 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 9.1 × 10^9/L, and C-reactive protein 30 mg/L.
Repeat blood count and C-reactive protein: Over three days of inpatient admission, CRP rose to 209 from 30, the white cell count remained normal, and there was no pyrexia.
Repeat pelvic ultrasound: The known left adnexal cyst was unchanged in size and appearance and measured 63 × 33 × 69 mm.
Repeat ultrasound Doppler and pelvic assessment: The whirlpool sign, ovarian stromal oedema, absence of detectable Doppler signals in the ovary, and free fluid in the pelvis were not observed.
Repeat abdominal examination: At 37 weeks and 1 day, pain increased and was associated with vomiting. Examination showed generalised tenderness and guarding in the left iliac fossa.
Intraoperative inspection of the adnexa: The left ovarian cyst was diffusely necrotic, twisted several times around its supporting ligaments, appeared blue-black, and formed a complex with the lateral third of the fallopian tube.

cases.case_summary: An 86-year-old woman was found unconscious by her family and transferred to the emergency department.
cases.full_text:
An 86-year-old woman was found unconscious by her family and transferred to the emergency department.
Medication history: No internal medication
Home environment: Lived in a non-air-conditioned room during scorching summer
Glasgow Coma Scale: Coma, score 6 (E1V1M4)
Body temperature: 42.4 °C
Blood pressure: 88/40 mmHg
Pulse rate: 120 beats/min
Laboratory data on arrival: WBC 15,200/μL; Hb 11.2 g/dL; Plt 75,000/μL; BUN 25.3 mg/dL; Cre 1.92 mg/dL; T-bil/D-bil 1.7/1.0 mg/dL; AST/ALT 194/49 U/L; CRP 0.08 mg/dL; PT-INR/APTT 1.60/34.7; FDP/D-dimer 74.51/31.07 μg/dL
Head MRI and MRA: No obvious abnormality

cases.case_summary: A 52-year-old man developed sudden-onset dyspnoea.
cases.full_text:
A 52-year-old man developed sudden-onset dyspnoea.
Medical history: No prior medical conditions and no regular prescription or over the counter medication; diffuse abdominal pain, obstipation, and weight loss of 8 kg over eight months
Abdominal computed tomography: Pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes and ascites
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.48, pO2 56 mmHg, pCO2 25 mmHg, base excess -3.3
Electrocardiogram: New-onset negative T waves in V1–V3
Echocardiography: Massively dilated right ventricle with reduced right ventricular function (TAPSE 1.5 cm) and estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure 70 mmHg
CT pulmonary angiogram: No signs of pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis; small areas of ground-glass densities throughout both lungs and bilateral pleural effusions
Perfusion/ventilation scintigraphy: Diffuse subtle perfusion defects throughout both lungs
Post-mortem lung examination: Poorly differentiated carcinoma tissue infiltrating the peripheral pulmonary microvasculature, with no embolic material in any proximal pulmonary arteries

cases.case_summary: A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a productive cough with blood-tinged sputum, pleuritic chest pain, and dyspnea for 2 days.
cases.full_text:
A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a productive cough with blood-tinged sputum, pleuritic chest pain, and dyspnea for 2 days.
Recent lung infection: Treated for a lung infection at a nearby health facility four months earlier.
Childhood chest infections: No prior history of recurring chest infections as a child.
Smoking history: No smoking history.
Vital signs: Heart rate 104 beats per minute, respiratory rate 30 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 86% while breathing room air, temperature 36.8 °C, and blood pressure 130/85 mmHg.
Chest examination: Crackles in the left posterior upper lung field.
Chest radiograph: Left upper lobe hyperlucency and ipsilateral small hila.
Chest computed tomography angiography: Left lung volume loss with hyperlucency, hypoplastic left pulmonary artery and veins, and diffuse varicoid and cystic bronchiectasis with superimposed bronchopneumonia.
CT angiography for pulmonary embolism and echocardiogram: Negative for pulmonary embolism; echocardiogram normal.

cases.case_summary: A 32-year-old Caucasian woman presents to endocrinology clinic with severe left knee pain and a significant genu valgum deformity in both knees.
cases.full_text:
A 32-year-old Caucasian woman presents to endocrinology clinic with severe left knee pain and a significant genu valgum deformity in both knees.
Childhood history: At age 9 she was told she may have had rickets, then was lost to follow-up.
Body size and parental heights: Height 155 cm, weight 58.5 kg, BMI 23.79 kg/m2; mother 173 cm and father 188 cm.
Fracture, dental, and family history: No fracture or abnormal dentition history, and no family history of rickets or other metabolic bone disease.
Current supplements: Taking over-the-counter vitamin D3 and no calcium supplementation.
Serum studies: Hypophosphatemia, elevated total vitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, undetectable FGF23, and low parathyroid hormone.
24-hour urine studies: Inappropriately normal phosphate excretion and normal urine calcium.
Renal ultrasound: Bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis without calculi.
Genetic testing: Homozygous SLC34A3 missense variant c.1402C>T (p.Arg468Trp), NM_080877.2.

cases.case_summary: A 91-year-old woman was transferred to the hospital with right upper abdominal pain.
cases.full_text:
A 91-year-old woman was transferred to the hospital with right upper abdominal pain.
Past medical history: Early gastric cancer treated with endoscopic mucosal resection 9 years earlier
Abdominal examination: Tenderness and distension in the upper abdomen, with rebound tenderness and muscle guarding
Blood tests: Other biochemical parameters within normal limits; white blood cells 12.9 × 10^3/μL and C-reactive protein 5.7 mg/dL
Abdominal computed tomography: Ascites, enhancement of the duodenal wall, and free air around the duodenum
Upper endoscopy: Perforation in the second portion of the duodenum
Intraoperative inspection: Perforated duodenal wall wrapped by omentum, with a tumor in the perforated wall
Histopathology of the resected specimen: Perforated duodenal diverticulum with pancreatic acinar cells, ducts, and islets of Langerhans in the submucosal layer around the diverticulum, without signs of inflammation

cases.case_summary: A 44-year-old woman presents to the hospital with six months of generalized weakness, a 40-pound weight loss over four months, and two weeks of progressively worsening dyspnea.
cases.full_text:
A 44-year-old woman presents to the hospital with six months of generalized weakness, a 40-pound weight loss over four months, and two weeks of progressively worsening dyspnea.
Antihypertensive history: Hypertension for five years, treated with lisinopril, with no use for over three years
Other medication history: No history of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, potassium-sparing diuretics, heparin, trimethoprim, or angiotensin receptor blockers
Admission serum electrolytes: Sodium 131 mM/l, potassium 5.7 mM/l, chloride 105 mM/l, bicarbonate 18 mM/l
Urine pH: 5 on day 4 of admission
Day 5 arterial blood gas and basic metabolic panel: Blood gas: pH 7.34, bicarbonate 14 mM/l, CO2 26 mmHg, pO2 96 mmHg. Panel: sodium 145 mM/l, potassium 5.5 mM/l, chloride 120 mM/l, bicarbonate 19 mM/l
Morning serum aldosterone: Less than 1 ng/dl
Urine and plasma electrolytes and osmolality: Urine sodium 59 mM/l, urine potassium 38 mM/l, urine osmolality 405 mOsm/kg, plasma potassium 5.1 mM/l, plasma osmolality 288 mOsm/kg; transtubular gradient 5.3
Serum cortisol: 14.4 μg/dl

cases.case_summary: A 61-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with bilateral knee swelling and pain, worse in the left knee, and difficulty bearing weight. She denied fever, chills, and malaise.
cases.full_text:
A 61-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with bilateral knee swelling and pain, worse in the left knee, and difficulty bearing weight. She denied fever, chills, and malaise.
Prior knee injection series: Multiple previous series of bilateral Hyalgan injections with no complications.
Current injection series and symptom onset: The first two bilateral Synvisc doses were tolerated; bilateral knee pain began 12 hours after the third set of injections.
Right knee examination: Range of motion 0–70 degrees because of pain, no erythema, mild suprapatellar effusion, and no pain with micromotion.
Left knee examination: Range of motion 0–30 degrees because of pain, no erythema, moderate suprapatellar effusion, and pain with micromotion.
Serum white blood cell count, CRP, and ESR: WBC 12.83 (4.5–11 normal), CRP 159 mg/L (0–10 normal), and ESR 79 mm/hr (0–40 normal).
Left knee aspiration: 38,580 WBC with a negative Gram stain and negative cultures.
Right knee aspiration: 29,670 WBC with a negative Gram stain and negative cultures.
Hospital day 4 blood counts and left-knee micromotion: CRP had fallen to 87.94 and WBC to 7.95, and the left leg no longer had pain with micromotion.

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old man was admitted with progressive dyspnea (NYHA class III).
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old man was admitted with progressive dyspnea (NYHA class III).
Past medical history: Chronic HCV-related liver disease
Chest radiograph: Signs of pulmonary congestion and a right basal pleural effusion
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction 60%, dilated right ventricle with normal systolic function, and no residual interventricular shunt
Course after diuretic therapy: Peripheral edema decreased and a repeat chest radiograph showed no pulmonary congestion, but dyspnea with low exercise tolerance persisted and oxygen was still required to maintain satisfactory oxygenation
Chest and abdomen CT: Small right pleural effusion, no signs of lung parenchymal disease or pulmonary embolism, cirrhotic liver disease with a focal lesion highly suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma, splenomegaly, and signs of portal hypertension
Right heart catheterization: High cardiac output, normal pulmonary vascular resistance, and only a slight increase in mean pulmonary pressure and wedge pressure
Microbubble transthoracic echocardiogram and 99mTc-MAA lung scintigraphy: Intrapulmonary right-to-left shunt
99mTc-MAA lung scintigraphy: Brain uptake 19%

cases.case_summary: A 39-year-old man with treated tuberculosis presented to the emergency department with two weeks of fever, generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, and generalized body aches, plus moderately severe nasal bleeding.
cases.full_text:
A 39-year-old man with treated tuberculosis presented to the emergency department with two weeks of fever, generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, and generalized body aches, plus moderately severe nasal bleeding.
Past medical history: Treated tuberculosis
Physical examination: Submandibular lymphadenopathy 2 × 1 cm and liver palpable 7 cm below the costal margin, with no gastrointestinal manifestations or skin lesions
Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 6.4 gm/dL, white blood cell count 1.7 × 10^3/μl, absolute neutrophil count 0.9 × 10^3/μl, and platelet count 2 × 10^3/μl
Peripheral blood smear: Marked leukopenia with 13% circulating medium-sized abnormal blastoid cells, fine nuclear chromatin, and unevenly distributed coarse deeply basophilic/metachromatic granules
Bone marrow aspirate: 26% atypical immature blast-like cells; most had eccentric nuclei, abundant cytoplasm, and coarse giant metachromatic/basophilic granules
Serum tryptase: 434.00 mcg/L (negative < 11 mcg/L)
Bone marrow immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD45, CD117, mast cell tryptase, CD25, CD43, and CD4; partially positive for CD30 and CD7; negative for CD2
Blood molecular analysis: KIT D816V mutation detected; BCR-ABL1 negative

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with two days of worsening heaviness in his right arm.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with two days of worsening heaviness in his right arm.
Recent illness history: A small cold or upper respiratory illness 3 weeks prior; no diarrhea, recent vaccinations, travel, or animal or farm contact
Right upper extremity strength: Uniform weakness with motor strength 3/5
Extremity reflexes and strength of the other limbs: Right upper extremity reflexes 1+; left upper extremity and both lower extremities strength 5/5 and reflexes 2+
Urine toxicology, head CT, brain MRI, and cervical spine imaging: No significant findings
Cerebrospinal fluid cell count and protein: 1 white blood cell, no red blood cells, and protein 33 mg/dL on hospital day 2
Motor and reflex examination on hospital day 4: Lower-limb strength spared until hospital day 4, when he could not walk unassisted; complete flaccid paralysis of the right upper extremity, left upper extremity strength 3/5, and complete areflexia in all extremities
Ocular, bulbar, sensory, and mental status findings during progression: No significant ophthalmoplegia, nystagmus, ptosis, dysphagia, sensory loss, or change in mentation; remained alert and orientated
Serum anti-GD1a antibody assay: Positive at 356 nm

cases.case_summary: An 81-year-old man is admitted with generalized edema and a rapid weight gain of 9.1 kg over the previous month.
cases.full_text:
An 81-year-old man is admitted with generalized edema and a rapid weight gain of 9.1 kg over the previous month.
Baseline serum creatinine and eGFR: Serum creatinine 123.76 μmol/L (1.4 mg/dL), with eGFR 47 mL/min/1.73 m² by CKD-EPI.
Laboratory studies two weeks before admission: Proteinuria 1661.1 mg/mmol (14.7 mg/mg), BUN 13.57 mmol/L (38 mg/dL), and serum creatinine 167.96 μmol/L (1.9 mg/dL).
Medication history: He denied recent NSAID or over-the-counter medication use. Sulindac had been used as needed, with the last dose thirteen months before presentation. Sildenafil was the only new medication.
History of edema onset: He reported an acute increase in peripheral and facial edema after a single dose of sildenafil four days before admission.
Serum chemistries on admission: Potassium 5.9 mmol/L (5.9 mEq/L), BUN 17.14 mmol/L (48 mg/dL), and serum creatinine 327.08 μmol/L (3.7 mg/dL).
Urinalysis and urine microscopy: Specific gravity 1.020, blood 4+, and protein 4+. Sediment showed 0–2 granular casts/lpf, no cellular casts/lpf, 0–5 nondysmorphic RBCs/hpf, and 0-1 WBC/hpf.
Renal ultrasound: Normal parenchyma in both kidneys, without hydronephrosis.
Renal biopsy tubulointerstitial histology: Patchy moderate interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils.

cases.case_summary: A 9-year-old boy presented to the dental department with a swelling in the right upper back tooth region for 3 months, initially small and gradually enlarging.
cases.full_text:
A 9-year-old boy presented to the dental department with a swelling in the right upper back tooth region for 3 months, initially small and gradually enlarging.
Associated symptoms: No pain, pus discharge, or other discomfort aside from unaesthetic facial asymmetry.
Extraoral examination: Diffuse, well-defined unilateral swelling about 4 × 3.5 cm on the right middle third of the face, from 1 cm below the infraorbital margin to the inferior border of the mandible, and from the ala of the nose to the anterior border of the ramus.
Palpation: Hard swelling with well-defined borders, without tenderness, local rise in temperature, or paresthesia.
Intraoral examination: Solitary, well-defined, unilateral ovoid swelling of the upper right buccal vestibule, about 4 cm × 3 cm, not crossing the midline.
Vestibular and palatal inspection: Obliteration of the buccal vestibule, buccal cortical expansion, and slight palatal expansion.
Intraoral periapical radiograph: Ground-glass trabecular pattern.
Cone-beam computed tomography: Expansion of the buccal and palatal cortical plates with a well-defined margin and a ground-glass trabecular pattern; more than half of the right maxillary sinus was involved.
Incisional biopsy microscopy: Irregularly shaped trabeculae of immature woven bone in a cellular, loosely arranged fibrous stroma; the trabeculae were not connected to each other and had no functional orientation.

cases.case_summary: A 65-year-old man presented with loss of appetite and malaise, followed by itching over the whole body, darkening of the urine, and yellowish discoloration of the eyes.
cases.full_text:
A 65-year-old man presented with loss of appetite and malaise, followed by itching over the whole body, darkening of the urine, and yellowish discoloration of the eyes.
Recent medication: Alfuzosin prolonged-release tablets were started at a dose of 10 mg given orally as a single dose.
Other medicines and liver disease history: No history of aspirin, paracetamol, or herbal medicine use, and no history of hepatic disease.
Liver tests before treatment: Liver tests were normal before the treatment.
Timing of symptoms: The illness began on the 9th day of therapy.
Serum liver biochemical tests: AST 175 U/L (reference 0–40), ALT 402 U/L (0–55), ALP 235 U/L (15–250), gamma-glutamyl transferase 327 U/L (8–61), total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2), and direct bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL (0–0.25).
Viral hepatitis studies: HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, anti-HAV IgM, anti-HEV, HEV-RNA, and HCV RNA were negative.
Autoimmune and metabolic liver tests: ANA, AMA, ASMA, LKM-1, transferrin saturation, ferritin, alpha-1 antitrypsin, ceruloplasmin, 24-hour urinary Cu2+, and Kayser-Fleischer ring examination were all normal.
Abdominal ultrasonography: The liver, gall bladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts were normal.

cases.case_summary: A 20-year-old girl presented with vulval swelling for 6 months. It had slowly increased in size and had been extremely painful for the last week.
cases.full_text:
A 20-year-old girl presented with vulval swelling for 6 months. It had slowly increased in size and had been extremely painful for the last week.
Vulval swelling: Swelling in the vulva for 6 months, slowly increasing in size, and extremely painful for the last one week.
Fever and vaginal discharge: No history of fever or vaginal discharge.
General examination: General condition fair, vital signs stable, afebrile, and no inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Local examination: Labial swelling on the left side with signs of inflammation.
Repeat vulval examination: A 5 × 5 cm swelling on the left labia majora, firm and not cystic, without signs of inflammation; labia minora not everted; hymen intact.
Operative findings: A firm encapsulated mass was enucleated along its capsular plane.
Gross pathology: Single nodular grey-white tissue mass weighing 56 g and measuring 6 × 4 × 3 cm; cut section showed grey-white areas, focal cystic areas, focal myxoid areas, and specks of hemorrhage.
Microscopy: Sheets and fascicles of oval to spindle shaped cells with abundant dense cytoplasm, microcystic areas, areas of hyalinization, and focal lymphocytic infiltrate.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 53-year-old Hispanic man presented to the emergency department with cough and non-massive hemoptysis.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 53-year-old Hispanic man presented to the emergency department with cough and non-massive hemoptysis.
Recent illness: Diagnosed with COVID-19 one month before this visit and did not require hospitalization.
Presentation: Recurrent cough, hemoptysis, and centralized chest pain for two weeks, with a progressively worsening cough, fatigue, generalized muscle pain, and loss of appetite. He denied fever, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He denied prior kidney disease, diabetes, tuberculosis exposure, drug abuse, tobacco, and alcohol use. He was tachycardic without acute distress, and the physical exam was unremarkable.
Admission blood counts and chemistries: White blood cell count 25.56 × 10^3/μL (reference 4.8–10.8), hemoglobin 14.7 g/dL (reference 12–16), BUN 107 mg/dL (reference 7–20), creatinine 5.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6–1.2), sodium 128 mmol/L (reference 136–145), and potassium 5.5 mmol/L (reference 3.5–5.1).
Chest CT: Multiple patchy consolidations throughout both lungs, some cavitating, located primarily at the periphery.
Infectious studies: Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR negative; Coccidioides antibody CF titer negative; Aspergillus antigen negative; Fungitell (1–3)-B-D-glucan negative; Blastomyces antibodies negative; acid-fast bacilli culture negative; hepatitis panel negative; HIV panel negative. The respiratory culture row lists yeast, with no growth listed as the normal value.
ANCA serology: ANCA assay positive. Proteinase antibody >100 U/mL (reference 0.0–3.5). Myeloperoxidase antibody 24.1 U/mL (reference 0.0–9.0). Cytoplasmic C-ANCA 1:320 (reference <1:20). Perinuclear P-ANCA <1:20 (reference <1:20).
Complement, ANA, and anti-GBM antibody: C3 56.9 mg/dL (reference 82.0–185.0) and C4 6.3 mg/dL (reference 15.0–53.0). Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody 5 (reference 0–20 U). Double-stranded anti-DNA antibody negative. Antinuclear antibody negative.
Lower-extremity skin examination: Diffuse, non-blanching, palpable hemorrhagic papules on both lower extremities; earlier petechial lesions there progressed to palpable purpura.

cases.case_summary: A 50-year-old man presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
cases.full_text:
A 50-year-old man presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
Pain characteristics: Colicky, sharp, stabbing pain that progressed to a constant dull discomfort, worse with coughing and deep inspiration
Trauma history: No history of trauma
Anticoagulation: Warfarin for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
INR: 3.8
Contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis: Well-defined ovoid mass 37 × 27 mm, attenuation 51 HU on both portal venous and delayed phases, with no washout; left adrenal normal Y shape; no evidence of cholecystitis; patchy right lower lobe consolidation
Symptom course: Over 12 hours the pain migrated from the right upper quadrant to the left flank
Repeat CT of the abdomen and pelvis: Persistent right adrenal mass 40 × 31 mm with attenuation 36 HU, and new left adrenal enlargement 34 × 24 mm with attenuation 25 HU
Adrenal protocol CT: No discrete adrenal mass; adrenal attenuation 40 HU and unchanged on pre-contrast, arterial, portal venous, and 10-minute delayed images, 1 week after the initial scan

cases.case_summary: A 67-year-old woman on a ventilator developed worsening respiratory status and hypotension on hospital day 7.
cases.full_text:
A 67-year-old woman on a ventilator developed worsening respiratory status and hypotension on hospital day 7.
Nasopharyngeal swab PCR: Positive PCR confirming COVID-19
Past history and medications: Diabetes mellitus, diabetic nephropathy requiring dialysis, angina, post-resection gastric cancer, postoperative spinal canal stenosis, and an antiplatelet agent
Coagulation studies on arrival: D-dimer 7.25 µg/mL, APTT 170 s, INR 1.35
Admission abdominal CT: No evident thromboembolism; edematous intestine, including the transverse colon; strong sclerotic changes of the abdominal vessels
Laboratory tests on hospital day 7: WBC 15,100/µl, CRP 32.14 mg/dL, D-dimer 26.51 µg/mL, APTT 47.2 s, PT-INR 1.24
Follow-up CT: Massive ascites, free air, and wall defects of the transverse colon
Laparotomy: Contaminated ascites, with 25 mm and 7 mm perforations on the right side of the transverse colon and necrotic tissue around them
Histopathology of the resected transverse colon: Mucosal necrosis around the perforation sites and microcirculatory thrombosis in the mesentery veins

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old woman is referred to the outpatient clinic with a 3-month history of left nasal obstruction, purulent nasal discharge, and facial pain that has not responded to multiple courses of oral antibiotics.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old woman is referred to the outpatient clinic with a 3-month history of left nasal obstruction, purulent nasal discharge, and facial pain that has not responded to multiple courses of oral antibiotics.
Past medical history: Diabetes mellitus.
Dental and facial trauma history: The patient did not relate any dental history or facial trauma history.
Nasal endoscopy: Purulent rhinorrhoea and a hypertrophic middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa, filling the nasal cavity and repressing the septum.
Oral cavity examination: No dental abnormality.
Paranasal sinus computed tomography: Heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion of the left middle turbinate filling the nasal cavity and repressing the septum; the ipsilateral maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses were entirely filled; no sinus wall erosion.
Intraoperative endoscopy: White lumps were present.
Histologic stains: Branching filaments with peripheral fibrinous and leukocytic exudate adjacent to suppurative infiltrates on hematoxylin and eosin, periodic acid–Schiff, and Grocott stains.
Histopathology: Actinomycetes were present.

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented to a university dental clinic with generalized bleeding from the gums and bad breath.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old woman presented to a university dental clinic with generalized bleeding from the gums and bad breath.
Orthodontic history: Orthodontic treatment 18 years earlier.
Color and cold testing of the maxillary central incisors: Both central incisors were normal in color and responded normally to cold testing.
Percussion and palpation of the maxillary central incisors: No discomfort, sensitivity, or swelling.
Periodontal probing of the maxillary central incisors: Probing depth was 5 mm on the palatal aspects of both central incisors.
Periapical radiographs of the maxillary central incisors: Areas of rarefaction in the cervical areas of the upper central incisors.
Mesially and distally shifted periapical radiographs: The lesion projection remained in the same position relative to the canal, and the canal outline was not disturbed.
Cone-beam computed tomography of the maxillary central incisors: Axial and sagittal sections showed radiolucent lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of the central incisors, extending from the external palatal surface and penetrating to perforate the pulp space.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 48-year-old man was found to have multiple liver tumors on abdominal ultrasonography during a routine medical examination.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 48-year-old man was found to have multiple liver tumors on abdominal ultrasonography during a routine medical examination.
Abdominal ultrasonography: Well-defined hypoechoic masses in segment 1 (67 × 53 mm), segment 6 (13 mm), and segment 2 (9 mm).
Serum liver biochemical tests: Total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL and albumin 4.2 g/dL, within normal ranges. Aspartate aminotransferase 37 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase 70 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 176 U/L, and gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase 170 IU/L, mildly increased.
Serum tumor markers: Alpha-fetoprotein 2.9 ng/ml, protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II 11 mAU/ml, and carcinoembryonic antigens 19-9 4.0 IU/L, all within normal limits.
Abdominal dynamic CT: Low-density 65-mm mass with an irregular margin on precontrast images, peripheral early ring enhancement in the arterial phase, and internal heterogeneous enhancement in the delayed phase.
EOB-MRI: Low signal intensity on T1-weighted images, several high-signal areas on T2-weighted images, and a hypointense mass in the hepatobiliary phase.
Diffusion-weighted MRI and ADC: Higher intensity than normal liver parenchyma on DWI at b value 1000. ADC 2.11 × 10−3 mm2/s in the peripheral area, 2.45 × 10−3 mm2/s in the central area, and mean 2.33 × 10−3 mm2/s.
FDG-PET: No accumulation of [18F]-FDG.
Pathology of the resected liver tumors: Segment 1 cut surface showed a 55 × 56 mm, well-demarcated, homogeneous, yellowish-white solid mass. The tumors were composed of various-sized irregularly dilated vessels with fibrous and hyalinized sclerotic stroma and CD34-positive vascular components.

cases.case_summary: At 19 weeks of gestation, after an uneventful pregnancy, obstetric ultrasound showed a sacrococcygeal mass with internal and external components measuring 34 × 28 mm.
cases.full_text:
At 19 weeks of gestation, after an uneventful pregnancy, obstetric ultrasound showed a sacrococcygeal mass with internal and external components measuring 34 × 28 mm.
Obstetric ultrasound: Sacrococcygeal mass with internal and external components, measuring 34 × 28 mm
Array comparative genomic hybridization: Normal
Echocardiogram: Normal
Fetal magnetic resonance imaging: At 22 weeks of gestation, a sacrococcygeal mass measured 60 × 70 × 57 mm, mixed and predominantly solid, with the largest cyst 40 mm, and without invasion or compression of the pelvic structures or coccyx
Follow-up ultrasound: Interval growth to 80 × 60 mm with profuse vascularization
Histologic examination: Predominant immature neuroepithelium
Histologic examination of mature elements: Mature cartilage, retinal pigmented epithelium, pancreatic tissue, and intestinal epithelium

findings.name: History of cerumen removal

findings.name: History of ear canal bony outgrowths

findings.name: Diving history

findings.name: Ear protection while diving

findings.name: High-resolution CT canal lumen

findings.name: High-resolution CT soft tissue and bone

draft.opening: A previously healthy 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sudden increase in dyspnea after one month of exertional dyspnea, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent fever, and develops acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest with pulseless electrical activity.
draft.opening_quote: The patient was a 25-year-old Hispanic woman of African descent. She was the youngest of four siblings, a nursing student, and worked part-time in the administrative department of the Cali City public transportation system. She was previously healthy, was a non-smoker, and did not consume alcohol or other drugs. Her father had arterial hypertension and her mother had type 2 diabetes. She had no other family history. The patient’s medical history included a 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent unquantified fever. She did not seek medical attention for these symptoms until she presented with a sudden increase in dyspnea, at which time she presented to the emergency department of a peripheral institution. Upon admission, she went into acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest, with pulseless electrical activity.
draft.diagnosis_quote: A diagnosis of GCRO was made (Figs. 3 and 4 ), with the origin apparently the thoracic vertebrae.

encounter.start: Emergency department presentation with sudden dyspnea and acute respiratory failure
encounter.cutoff: Histologic diagnosis on biopsy during the same admission
encounter.cutoff_quote: A diagnosis of GCRO was made (Figs. 3 and 4 ), with the origin apparently the thoracic vertebrae.

findings.name: Recent symptom history
findings.result: One-month history of dyspnea on exertion, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent unquantified fever.
findings.quote: The patient’s medical history included a 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and intermittent unquantified fever.

findings.name: Emergency department course
findings.result: Acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest with pulseless electrical activity; difficult to ventilate despite orotracheal intubation.
findings.quote: Upon admission, she went into acute respiratory failure and cardiorespiratory arrest, with pulseless electrical activity. Despite orotracheal intubation, the patient was difficult to ventilate.

findings.name: Vital signs on arrival
findings.result: Blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36 °C, and oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support.
findings.quote: Her vital signs were: blood pressure, 200/140 mmHg; heart rate, 100 beats per minute; respiratory rate, 16 breaths per minute; temperature, 36 °C; oxygen saturation, 78% despite being on ventilatory support.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm), thick neck with jugular engorgement and no masses, no skin lesions, sinus tachycardia, bilateral thick rales, and no abdominal collateral circulation, ascites, masses, or extremity edema.
findings.quote: Physical examination revealed pupils with anisocoria (right 5 mm, left 3 mm) and thick neck with jugular engorgement with no masses. There were no skin lesions. The cardiopulmonary evaluation revealed sinus tachycardia, and on auscultation of the lung, bilateral thick rales were found. There was no collateral circulation, ascites, or masses on the abdomen. Extremities were without edema.

findings.name: Chest radiography
findings.result: Homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the airway to the left.
findings.quote: A chest radiography (X-ray) was performed, showing a homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass that compressed and displaced the airway (Fig. 1 ) to the left.

findings.name: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy
findings.result: Extrinsic compression at the distal end of the orotracheal tube, with no endotracheal or endobronchial lesions.
findings.quote: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy was then performed, in which extrinsic compression was observed at the distal end of the orotracheal tube, with no evidence of endotracheal or endobronchial lesions.

findings.name: Chest and neck CT
findings.result: Lobulated solid mass in the right thoracic operculum, 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm, described as seeming to originate in the pleura, with a 27 × 28 mm nodular component on the mediastinal pleura; mass effect on the right pulmonary hilum, right supra-aortic trunks, and superior vena cava; pneumomediastinum and left pneumothorax; lytic involvement of the T1 and T2 vertebral bodies, pedicles, and transverse processes with anterior cortical fracture.
findings.quote: Evaluations were continued with a chest and neck computerized tomography (CT) scan, revealing a large, lobulated, and solid mass, with well-defined contours, located in the right thoracic operculum that seemed to originate in the pleura and measured 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm (L×AP×T). The mass had a nodular component attached to the mediastinal pleura, measuring 27 × 28 mm, which seemed to be thickened. A mass effect of the right pulmonary hilum, right supra-aortic trunks, and superior vena cava were reported. There was a presence of pneumomediastinum and left pneumothorax. Also, lytic bone involvement of the body, pedicle, and transverse processes of the first and second thoracic ( T1 and T2) vertebrae was observed, with a fracture of the bone cortex through the anterior portion of the vertebrae.

findings.name: Biopsy histopathology
findings.result: Mesenchymal lesion with abundant randomly arranged osteoclast-type giant cells with round nuclei and mild pleomorphism; spindle cells with cytological atypia, an increased nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, and abundant mitoses; isolated osteoid; tumor and ischemic necrosis; no normal bone; Ki-67 index 18%; phosphorylated histone H3 with three mitoses per high-power field.
findings.quote: Histologically, a mesenchymal neoplastic lesion was observed with abundant giant osteoclastic cells with round nuclei and mild pleomorphism. The cells were randomly arranged. Similar to stromal tissue, the lesion presented spindle cells with cytological atypia, an increased nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, and abundant mitosis. Osteoid material was found in isolation, with areas of tumor and ischemic necrosis. No normal bone tissue was observed; the Ki-67 proliferation index was 18%, and the phosphorylated histone H3 (PHH3) proliferation marker was present with three mitoses per high power field (HPF).

encounter.cutoff_quote: After histologic evaluation a diagnosis of multilocular peritoneal inclusion cyst (benign cystic mesothelioma) was given.

findings.name: Past medical and surgical history
findings.result: Hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, and cesarean section with bilateral tubal ligation; no smoking history; family history noncontributory.
findings.quote: Past medical and surgical history was significant for hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, and cesarean section with bilateral tubal ligation. She had no smoking history and family medical history was noncontributory.

findings.name: Abdominal examination
findings.result: Vital signs within normal limits; abdomen distended and diffusely tender.
findings.quote: On physical exam, vital signs were within normal limits and the abdomen was distended and diffusely tender.

findings.name: Pelvic examination
findings.result: A 30 cm adnexal mass; the uterus was small and difficult to palpate because of the mass.
findings.quote: Pelvic exam was significant for a 30 cm adnexal mass. The uterus was small and difficult to palpate secondary to the large adnexal mass.

findings.name: Transvaginal and transabdominal ultrasound with color Doppler
findings.result: Large pelvic mass, described as likely arising from the left ovary and extending to the first intercostal space; multiloculated complex mass with multiple thick septations measuring 24 × 18 cm; moderate pelvic free fluid; anteverted uterus of normal appearance with a thin endometrial lining; right ovary 3.9 × 3.3 × 3.5 cm with a 3 cm simple cyst.
findings.quote: Findings were notable for a large pelvic mass likely originating in the left ovary and extending to the level of the first intercostal space. The mass was described as a multiloculated complex with multiple thick septations measuring 24 × 18 cm ( Figure 1 ). Moderate free fluid was also noted in the pelvis. The uterus was anteverted and normal in appearance with a thin endometrial lining. The right ovary measured 3.9 × 3.3 × 3.5 cm with a 3 cm simple cyst.

findings.name: Computed tomography
findings.result: A 28.3 × 24.4 × 16.3 cm predominantly cystic mass extending from the pelvis to the upper abdomen, with superior displacement of the bowel.
findings.quote: Computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a 28.3 × 24.4 × 16.3 cm predominantly cystic mass extending from the pelvis to the upper abdomen with displacement of the bowel superiorly

findings.name: CA125
findings.result: Value of 95, reported as significantly elevated.
findings.quote: CA125 was significantly elevated, with a value of 95.

findings.name: Intraoperative findings
findings.result: Uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries were normal. A 26–28 cm multiloculated peritoneal cyst arose from the left cornual region of the uterine fundus on a wide pedicle, with significant adhesions to the ureters, omentum, and pelvic sidewall. Three liters of cystic fluid were evacuated.
findings.quote: Surgical findings included a normal uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The large 26–28 cm multiloculated peritoneal cyst was noted to be originating from the left cornual region of the uterine fundus from a wide pedicle ( Figure 1 ). There were significant adhesions involving the cyst, ureters, omentum, and pelvic sidewall. Three liters of cystic fluid was evacuated and sent for cytology.

findings.name: Cyst fluid cytology
findings.result: Reactive benign mesothelial cells.
findings.quote: Cytology was significant for reactive benign mesothelial cells.

encounter.cutoff_quote: Microscopic tissue examination showed fragments of trabecular bony structure with bony sequestrum alongside new bone formation and necrosis, and therefore, KD was confirmed.

findings.name: Recent back pain and trauma history
findings.result: No history of significant trauma; minor back pain began after pulling a rug one month earlier.
findings.quote: The patient had no history of actual trauma and had only suffered from minor back pain, after pulling a rug a month prior.

findings.name: Back and leg symptom course
findings.result: Pain that was initially mild gradually became severely disabling, with progressive weakness and diffuse paresthesia in both legs.
findings.quote: Although the pain was initially low in severity, it had gradually increased in intensity and lead to severe disability and progressive weakness in both legs. He also complained of diffuse paresthesia in both legs.

findings.name: Standing, lower-limb strength, and sphincter function
findings.result: He could hardly stand. Big-toe extensors were weak bilaterally (severe on the left, moderate on the right), and ankle dorsiflexors were moderately weak on both sides. Sphincter function was intact. Ankle plantar flexors and quadriceps had normal power.
findings.quote: On physical examination, the patient could hardly stand. Manual muscle testing revealed a bilateral weakness in the extensor muscles of the big toe (severe on the left and moderate on the right) and ankle dorsiflexors (moderate on both sides), but sphincter function remained intact. The power of the ankle plantar flexors and quadriceps were also completely normal.

findings.name: Laboratory testing

encounter.start: Emergency department presentation with bilateral knee swelling and pain
encounter.cutoff: Discharge on hospital day 5
encounter.cutoff_quote: On hospital day five the patient was discharged with very strict return precautions.

findings.name: Prior knee injection series
findings.result: Multiple previous series of bilateral Hyalgan injections with no complications.
findings.quote: She also had received multiple series of bilateral Hyalgan® (Fidia, Florham Park, NJ) injections in the past with no complications.

findings.name: Current injection series and symptom onset
findings.result: The first two bilateral Synvisc doses were tolerated; bilateral knee pain began 12 hours after the third set of injections.
findings.quote: The patient had begun a series of Synvisc (Sanofi, Cambridge, MA) injections for which she had tolerated the first two doses bilaterally well. She underwent her third set of Synvisc injections and began having pain bilaterally 12 h after injection.

findings.name: Right knee examination
findings.result: Range of motion 0–70 degrees because of pain, no erythema, mild suprapatellar effusion, and no pain with micromotion.
findings.quote: Her right knee exam was as follows: range of motion from 0–70 degrees secondary to pain, no erythema, mild suprapatellar effusion present, no pain with micromotion.

findings.name: Left knee examination
findings.result: Range of motion 0–30 degrees because of pain, no erythema, moderate suprapatellar effusion, and pain with micromotion.

findings.name: Serum white blood cell count, CRP, and ESR
findings.result: WBC 12.83 (4.5–11 normal), CRP 159 mg/L (0–10 normal), and ESR 79 mm/hr (0–40 normal).
findings.quote: Her white blood cell count (WBC) was 12.83 (4.5–11 normal), her C-reactive protein (CRP) level was 159 mg/L (0–10 normal), her erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 79 mm/hr (0–40 normal).

findings.name: Left knee aspiration
findings.result: 38,580 WBC with a negative Gram stain and negative cultures.
findings.quote: Her left knee aspirate yielded 38,580 WBC with a negative gram stain and negative cultures.

findings.name: Right knee aspiration
findings.result: 29,670 WBC with a negative Gram stain and negative cultures.
findings.quote: Her right knee aspirate yielded 29,670 WBC with a negative gram stain and negative cultures.

findings.name: Hospital day 4 blood counts and left-knee micromotion
findings.result: CRP had fallen to 87.94 and WBC to 7.95, and the left leg no longer had pain with micromotion.
findings.quote: By her fourth day in the hospital, her CRP had dropped to 87.94 and her WBC had dropped to 7.95. She no longer had any pain with micromotion in her left leg.

findings.result: Well-defined hypoechoic masses in segment 1 (67 × 53 mm), segment 6 (13 mm), and segment 2 (9 mm).

findings.result: Total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL and albumin 4.2 g/dL, within normal ranges. Aspartate aminotransferase 37 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase 70 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 176 U/L, and gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase 170 IU/L, mildly increased.
